message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling (both under her own name and her pseudonym Robert Galbraith):

| Title | Year | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | The first book in the globally‑famous Harry Potter series. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; introduces the Chamber of Secrets plot. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry’s interference. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; reveals Voldemort’s backstory and the Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Final book; concludes the epic saga. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel published under her own name; a political drama set in a small town. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable released as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut crime novel in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Ink Black** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2022 | Fifth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |

These titles cover the breadth of Rowling’s work—from the beloved wizarding world to her ventures into adult fiction and crime thrillers.
